articles.title: How to evaluate text-to-speech voices before you ship them
articles.excerpt: Picking a voice for a product usually goes like this: open the provider's demo page, type "Hello, how are you today?", listen to six voices, pick the one that sounds nicest. Then the voice goes into a…
articles.body: Picking a voice for a product usually goes like this: open the provider's demo page, type "Hello, how are you today?", listen to six voices, pick the one that sounds nicest. Then the voice goes into a support agent that has to read order numbers, or a narrator that has to get through Urdu place names, and it falls apart. Or it sounds right but takes two seconds before anything plays, which in a conversation feels like forever. I built Signal Tank to make that choice with evidence. You write or pick a real script, choose a voice and settings, generate a take, and every take is saved next to its numbers so you can compare them side by side. The code is small and public, and the patterns in it apply to any TTS provider.

Most developers were able to get their workflows running on the first try and put the compiled SQL straight to use. The most frequently praised features were that the generated SQL didn’t invent column names, every step could be inspected, and even old queries that they had once dared not touch could now be reworked. But we also received plenty of negative feedbacks, some of it quite pointed. These pain points weren’t all the same, so we grouped them into two categories. Some capabilities aren’t clearly explained in the documentation.

articles.title: Why Compressing a PDF Sometimes Makes It Bigger (and What Ghostscript's -dPDFSETTINGS Does)
articles.excerpt: One of the more confusing bug reports I get on my file tools goes like this: "I compressed my PDF and it got bigger." The first time I saw it I assumed a bug. It wasn't. Some PDFs are already about as…
articles.body: One of the more confusing bug reports I get on my file tools goes like this: "I compressed my PDF and it got bigger." The first time I saw it I assumed a bug. It wasn't. Some PDFs are already about as small as they can get, and running them through a compressor that rebuilds the file can add bytes rather than remove them. Here's why that happens, what Ghostscript's presets actually change, and how I decide which approach to use. What takes up space in a PDF Before compressing anything, it helps to know what you're compressing. In most real-world PDFs, the size comes from three things: Images. Scans, photos and screenshots. In a scanned document they're nearly the whole file. Fonts. Embedded font programs, sometimes complete fonts rather than just the glyphs that are used.
articles.author: OneFileKit

articles.title: How I run Claude Code and Codex as writer and reviewer, with a forced verdict line
articles.excerpt: Codex reviews each Claude Code commit in a read-only sandbox, and any review that doesn't end on Verdict: ACCEPT or Verdict: CHANGES REQUIRED counts as failed. So does a crash. The merge check in my f…
articles.body: Codex reviews each Claude Code commit in a read-only sandbox, and any review that doesn't end on Verdict: ACCEPT or Verdict: CHANGES REQUIRED counts as failed. So does a crash. The merge check in my free gate also refuses an ACCEPT that came from the engine that wrote the code. The writer answers every finding, each new commit gets a fresh review, and later the roles swap so each engine spends time on both sides of the diff. This is the setup I use on my own projects, with the CLI flags taken from the official Claude Code and Codex docs. The reasons I use Claude Code and Codex together are in an earlier post. 1. Give each engine one job Claude Code is the default writer. Writing is where context piles up: the plan, the files touched, the tests run.

articles.body: "Trong lập trình hướng đối tượng, tính đa hình (Polymorphism) là một nguyên lý quan trọng cho phép một đối tượng thể hiện các hành vi khác nhau tùy thuộc vào ngữ cảnh. Điều này giúp tăng tính linh hoạt và mở rộng khả năng của chương trình. Dưới đây là những điều cơ bản bạn cần biết về tính đa hình trong Java." Ⅰ. Đa hình (Polymorphism) là gì? Tính đa hình (polymorphism) là một trong bốn tính chất cơ bản của lập trình hướng đối tượng (OOP) trong Java, bên cạnh tính đóng gói (encapsulation), tính kế thừa (inheritance) và tính trừu tượng (abstraction). Tính đa hình cho phép một đối tượng có thể thực hiện các hành động (phương thức) theo nhiều cách khác nhau.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.body: On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes.

articles.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
articles.excerpt: New research suggests that Little Red Dots, which have puzzled astronomers since the JWST began discovering them, could host primordial black holes born during the Big Bang.
articles.body: Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium.

articles.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
articles.excerpt: "*sshole" poses a serious threat to Internet security.
articles.body: Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting. The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Four days later, the prediction shows signs of becoming real.

articles.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
articles.excerpt: Starfish Space's first Otter servicing spacecraft suffered a glitch in orbit recently, ending its technology-demonstrating mission for NASA.
articles.body: Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short.
